A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WikiAutoGen/WikiSeek work, with readable main text, tables, and figures. However, both end with references despite mentioning appendices. V2 additionally assigns evaluator-validation results to an absent Appendix B, limiting comparison of those analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original WikiSeek benchmark experiments, component ablations, difficulty analyses, and a human evaluation in Tables 2–4 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds a commercial-system comparison with quality scores and generation times in Table 5.

M1.justification: The outline generation, persona-based knowledge exploration, multi-perspective self-reflection, and multimodal article-writing procedures remain unchanged. Sections 4.2–4.5 retain the same retrieval, CLIP top-three selection, and refinement steps; wording changes do not establish a procedural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 300-topic WikiSeek benchmark, three difficulty groups, and text-only, image-only, and image-text inputs. The human study retains 100 text-only topics. The commercial comparison uses existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 retain oRAG, Storm, Co-Storm, and OmniThink. V2 adds a substantial comparison category in Table 5: commercial systems labeled OpenAI, Google, and Grok. OpenAI and Grok have results for all three input modalities; Google has text-only results.

E3.justification: The original GPT-4o evaluation and human-study settings remain unchanged. V2 adds Prometheus2 judging and generation-time comparisons for the commercial experiment. Section 5.1 also announces Gemini2.5-Flash validation, but its detailed protocol is assigned to the unavailable Appendix B.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3 and difficulty analysis in Figure 3 are unchanged. V2 announces additional validation using alternative evaluators, but the referenced Appendix B is absent, preventing verification of the scope and evidence of this potential robustness extension.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF adds generation-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both human-study descriptions specify three independent participants per topic.

E6.justification: V2 adds distinct commercial quality-and-speed results in Table 5, including Prometheus2 averages of 89.01 for WikiAutoGen, 93.06 for OpenAI, and 85.06 for Grok. These are new comparisons under another evaluator, not improvements over Table 2 scores. Tables 2–4 and Figures 3–4 retain their values. The human-study text changes from 99% to 97.7%, correcting it to match Figure 4 in both versions.

T1.justification: The task formulation and persona-count condition remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies substantive theoretical results, proofs, or derivations that change between versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: WikiSeek, multimodal WikiAutoGen, and multi-perspective self-reflection. The main 8%–29% textual-improvement claim is unchanged; the commercial experiment is not incorporated into these principal contribution statements.

C2.justification: New Section 5.4 interprets the commercial timing comparison as evidence of scalability and suitability for time-sensitive applications. Section 2 also newly attributes niche-domain weaknesses to scarce structured prior knowledge. Existing interpretations of component contributions and difficulty robustness remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes an examples-only website pointer into a statement that code and examples are available. V2 names additional evaluators and reports approximate generation times, including eight minutes for WikiAutoGen. Existing DSPy, model assignments, Serper retrieval, temperature, and top-p details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 removes the entire RAG/MRAG related-work discussion and twelve cited works, including MuRAG, REALM, dense passage retrieval, and EchoSight, eliminating a substantial branch of research positioning. It retains the expository-writing and self-reflection discussions, explicitly calls WikiAutoGen the first multimodal writing system, and adds the Prometheus 2 reference.

P1.justification: Paragraphs are extensively rewritten or condensed across the introduction, related work, benchmark description, method, results, and conclusion. Structural changes include removing the RAG discussion and inserting the commercial-comparison subsection before human evaluation. Terminology, grammar, headings, and author affiliations are also edited.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 5, relocates Figure 3 from PDF page 8 to page 7, highlights the full-model row in Table 3, and adjusts spacing and captions. Existing figures and table structures are otherwise largely preserved.

improvement.justification: V2 improves prose, corrects the human-study percentage, and adds potentially useful commercial comparisons. However, Section 5.4 calls OpenAI the fastest commercial baseline despite Table 5 listing 30 minutes versus Google's 12 and Grok's 10, and compares Google's text-only score with multimodal averages. The absent Appendix B also prevents checking the advertised evaluator validation. These reporting problems and unavailable evidence prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
